root_cause.text: The driver incorrectly tied device-managed resources (SPI controller allocation and DMA buffers) to the parent USB device (`&udev->dev`) instead of the USB interface device (`&intf->dev`), causing resource leaks and improper lifetime management when the driver is unbound without device disconnection (e.g., on probe deferral or configuration changes).
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows all `devm_spi_alloc_host` and `devm_kzalloc` calls changed from `&udev->dev` to `&intf->dev`. The commit message explicitly states: "USB drivers bind to USB interfaces and any device managed resources should have their lifetime tied to the interface rather than parent USB device. This avoids issues like memory leaks when drivers are unbound without their devices being physically disconnected."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix SPI controller device binding to use USB interface instead of USB device in ch341 probe.
intent_record.what: Changed the first argument of devm_spi_alloc_host from &udev->dev to &intf->dev in ch341_probe.
intent_record.how: The SPI controller is now allocated with the USB interface device as its parent, ensuring proper resource lifecycle management tied to the interface rather than the USB device.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory resource management by tying the rx_buf allocation to the interface device lifetime.
intent_record.what: In ch341_probe, changed the device argument of devm_kzalloc from &udev->dev to &intf->dev.
intent_record.how: The allocated memory is now associated with the USB interface device instead of the USB device, ensuring automatic freeing when the interface is removed or driver unbinds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix devm resource lifetime by using the correct device (interface device) for tx_buf allocation in ch341_probe.
intent_record.what: Changed the device pointer in devm_kzalloc for tx_buf allocation from &udev->dev to &intf->dev, also condensed the declaration from two lines to one.
intent_record.how: The memory allocation for the transmit buffer is now associated with the USB interface device instead of the USB device, ensuring the buffer is properly freed when the interface is unbound or the driver is removed.
